definition_en: inflammation of the lining of the intestine, often causing pain and diarrhoea
core_image: 肠壁内侧发红肿胀，像被热水烫过的管道内壁
scene: 幼犬连续两天腹泻，兽医在化验后确诊为肠炎。 The puppy was treated for enteritis after two days of diarrhoea.
sceneCN: 这里 enteritis 是「肠炎」（第 1 个义项：肠道黏膜的炎症）；句意：这只幼犬在接受肠炎治疗。

senses.title: Inflammation of the intestine
senses.definition: a medical condition in which the wall of the intestine becomes inflamed and painful
senses.definitionCN: 肠壁发炎并伴疼痛的疾病状态
senses.example: Enteritis can follow a bacterial infection.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌感染之后可能引发肠炎。
senses.why: The name is built from the Greek word for intestine plus the inflammation ending used across medicine.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示肠的希腊语加上医学通用的炎症词尾构成。

senses.title: A named disease in young animals or infants
senses.definition: a specific inflammatory disease, often necrotising, that affects neonates and livestock
senses.definitionCN: 多发于新生幼崽与家畜的特定炎症性疾病，常伴组织坏死
senses.example: Necrotising enteritis is a risk in premature babies.
senses.exampleCN: 坏死性肠炎是早产儿面临的风险之一。
senses.why: Veterinary and neonatal usage narrows the general name to one recognised syndrome.
senses.whyCN: 兽医与新生儿医学把泛称收窄为一种公认病症。

senses.title: A combining element in compound disease names
senses.titleCN: 构词成分；复合病名后缀
senses.definition: the element -itis attached to entero- inside compounds such as gastroenteritis
senses.definitionCN: entero- 与炎症词尾 -itis 在胃肠炎等复合词中的构词成分
senses.example: Gastroenteritis combines the stomach and gut names.
senses.exampleCN: gastroenteritis 把胃与肠的名称合为一体。
senses.why: Because the parts are productive, the same shape reappears wherever a gut inflammation must be named.
senses.whyCN: 由于这两个成分都能产新词，凡需命名肠道炎症时同一形态都会再现。

intro.en: The word joins a Greek noun for intestine with a Greek ending that medicine uses for inflammation.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示肠的希腊名词与医学表炎症的希腊词尾拼在一起。

items.en: Enteron means gut or intestine.
items.cn: enteron 指肠道。

items.en: The ending itis marked a pathological condition.
items.cn: 词尾 -itis 标记病变状态。

items.en: Medical Latin wrote enteritis as a fixed diagnostic term.
items.cn: 近代拉丁医学文书把 enteritis 写成固定诊断术语。

items.en: English clinical texts adopt the word alongside gastritis.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语临床文本采纳该词，与 gastritis 并用。

items.en: Veterinary usage extends it to named syndromes in animals.
items.cn: 现代英语中兽医用法把它延伸到动物特定病症。

note.en: Group one holds the same-ending inflammation names; group two holds close clinical terms.
note.cn: 第一组是同一炎症词尾的病名；第二组是相近的临床说法。

entries.definition: The same ending applied to the stomach rather than the intestine.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词尾用于胃而非肠。

entries.definition: Inflammation limited to the colon, a narrower site than the general gut term.
entries.definitionCN: 炎症限于结肠，部位比泛称更窄。

entries.definition: Named for the lower small intestine specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 专指小肠下段的炎症。

entries.definition: Relating to the intestines, as in an enteric coating.
entries.definitionCN: 肠的，如肠溶包衣。

entries.definition: The body's response itself, without locating the organ.
entries.definitionCN: 机体的炎症反应本身，不定位器官。

entries.definition: Invasion by germs, which may lead to the inflammation but is not the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 病原体侵入，可引发炎症但并非同一概念。

entries.definition: The combined condition, common in everyday travel advice.
entries.definitionCN: 胃肠同时发炎，常见于旅行健康提示。

entries.definition: A long-term clinical category rather than a single acute episode.
entries.definitionCN: 长期临床类别，而非一次急性发作。

normalIntro.en: Split the word into entero, gut, and itis, the medical ending for inflammation.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 entero（肠）与 itis（医学炎症词尾）。

normal.en: Every -itis word names one inflamed place: joint, stomach, gut.
normal.cn: 所有 -itis 词都指某一部位发炎：关节、胃、肠。

normal.en: Enteritis is usually uncountable, so no plural is needed.
normal.cn: enteritis 通常不可数，无需复数。

normal.en: Travel writing prefers gastroenteritis, which adds the stomach.
normal.cn: 旅行类文章更常用 gastroenteritis，其中加入了胃。

normal.en: Veterinary reports say necrotising enteritis for the severe form.
normal.cn: 兽医报告用 necrotising enteritis 表示重症。

normal.en: Do not confuse enteric the adjective with enteritis the disease.
normal.cn: 不要混淆形容词 enteric 与病名 enteritis。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe whose inner wall has turned red and swollen.
abstract.cn: 想象一段管道，内壁已经发红肿胀。

abstract.en: Imagine a diagram of the gut lit up in warning colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一张肠道示意图被警示色点亮。

abstract.en: Think of a fever chart whose label ends in the same four letters.
abstract.cn: 想想体温记录单上以同样四个字母结尾的标签。

examples.en: The child was hospitalised with severe enteritis.
examples.cn: 这个孩子因重症肠炎住院。

examples.en: Bacterial enteritis spreads through contaminated water.
examples.cn: 细菌性肠炎经污染水源传播。

examples.en: Rest and fluids are the standard care for enteritis.
examples.cn: 休息与补液是肠炎的常规护理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安肠赖提死」——肠道不安宁拖累人，所以 enteritis 是肠炎；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 ἕντερον / enteron（肠）＋ -itis（炎症）→ 近代拉丁医学语 enteritis → 现代英语 enteritis，核心义「肠道发炎」。

sensesIntro.en: The term names an inflamed gut, narrows to specific syndromes, and works as a productive element in compound disease names.
sensesIntro.cn: 该词既指肠道发炎，也可收窄为特定病症，还能作为构词成分进入复合病名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the inner lining of the intestine reddened and swollen.
core.cn: 核心意象：肠内壁发红肿胀。

branches.en: The clinical name for an inflamed intestine.
branches.cn: 肠炎的临床名称。

branches.en: Specialised fields attach a named syndrome to it.
branches.cn: 专门领域为它附上具体病症名。

branches.en: The parts keep building new compound names.
branches.cn: 两个成分继续构造新的复合病名。

branches.en: Both share the idea of inflamed gut tissue.
branches.cn: 两者都以肠壁组织发炎为核心。

branches.en: Severe forms and compounds appear together in veterinary texts.
branches.cn: 重症与复合词在兽医文献中并见。

intro.en: This is a wholly classical build: a Greek combining form plus a Greek medical ending.
intro.cn: 这是完全古典语构成的词：希腊组合形式加希腊医学词尾。

latinIntro.en: Medical Latin wrote enteron and -itis unchanged, which is how the parts reached English textbooks.
latinIntro.cn: 医学拉丁语原样书写 enteron 与 -itis，这两个成分由此进入英语教材。

items.example: Entero- opens enteropathy.
items.exampleCN: entero- 位于 enteropathy 开头。

items.example: Enteron is the base of the name.
items.exampleCN: enteron 是该病名的基础。

items.example: The ending forms arthritis.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 arthritis。

items.example: Enteric coating dissolves in the gut.
items.exampleCN: 肠溶包衣在肠内溶解。

items.example: Gastro- plus -itis gives gastroenteritis.
items.exampleCN: gastro- 加 -itis 构成 gastroenteritis。

items.example: A close structural neighbour.
items.exampleCN: 结构上邻近的词。

items.example: Colitis names a narrower site.
items.exampleCN: colitis 指明更窄的部位。

items.example: The ending -cyte means cell.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cyte 意为细胞。

items.example: It qualifies the severe form.
items.exampleCN: 该形容词修饰重症类型。

definition_zh: 探索；勘探；探究；考察；探查
definition_en: the act of travelling through or investigating an unknown area, subject, or system
core_image: 一束手电光在黑暗洞穴里向前扫，光圈之外仍是未画上地图的空白。
scene: 探测器着陆后，团队把第一批地形数据称为探索，而不是测绘。 After the lander touches down the team calls the first terrain data exploration rather than mapping, because nobody knows what will turn up.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 exploration 是「对未知区域的探索」（第 1、3 个义项）；句意：探测器着陆后，团队把第一批地形数据称为探索而不是测绘，因为还不知道会发现什么。

pos.zh: 探索；勘探；探究；考察；（医学）探查

senses.title: Travel into the unknown
senses.titleCN: 探索：走进没有地图的地方
senses.definition: the act of travelling through an unknown region to find out what is there
senses.definitionCN: 穿越未知地区以查明那里有什么的行为
senses.example: The exploration of the upper river took three seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 对上游河流的探索花了三个季节。
senses.why: The word begins with space: someone moves into ground where no account yet exists, and the account is made by moving.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从空间开始：有人走进尚无记录的地方，而记录是靠行走做出来的。

senses.title: Investigation of a subject
senses.titleCN: 探究：把未知的问题一点点打开
senses.definition: the systematic investigation of a subject, question, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某主题、问题或观念的系统探究
senses.example: Her exploration of the archive changed the accepted chronology.
senses.exampleCN: 她对档案的探究改变了公认的年表。
senses.why: The unknown here is intellectual rather than geographical. The explorer still moves without a map, but the terrain is made of records and questions.
senses.whyCN: 这里的未知是智识性的，而非地理性的。探索者仍在地图之外移动，但地形由记录与问题构成。

senses.title: Space exploration
senses.titleCN: 太空探索：把探测器送到未知环境
senses.definition: the investigation of space by probes, robots, or crewed missions
senses.definitionCN: 通过探测器、机器人或载人任务对太空进行考察
senses.example: Space exploration has mapped the surface of every planet.
senses.exampleCN: 太空探索已绘制了每颗行星的表面。
senses.why: The traveller is a machine and the report comes back as data. The unknown is extreme, so the exploration is designed before it is lived.
senses.whyCN: 旅行者是机器，报告以数据返回。未知极端到必须先设计探索，再‘经历’它。

senses.title: Surgical exploration
senses.titleCN: 医学探查：打开身体以查明情况
senses.definition: a medical procedure in which a body area is examined, often surgically, to find the cause of symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 为查明症状原因而对身体某部位进行检查、常为手术性的程序
senses.example: The surgeon performed an exploration of the abdomen.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生对腹腔进行了探查。
senses.why: The unknown is inside the body. Exploration is justified when imaging cannot answer the question, so seeing directly becomes the test.
senses.whyCN: 未知在身体内部。当影像无法回答问题时，探查就有理由：直接看见成为检验。

senses.title: Resource exploration
senses.titleCN: 资源勘探：寻找可开采的矿藏
senses.definition: the search for mineral, oil, gas, or water resources underground
senses.definitionCN: 在地下寻找矿产、石油、天然气或水资源
senses.example: Oil exploration in the basin began with seismic surveys.
senses.exampleCN: 该盆地的石油勘探从地震勘测开始。
senses.why: Here the unknown is what lies below, and the goal is not knowledge but a find. Exploration ends when a resource is located, not when the map is complete.
senses.whyCN: 这里未知在地下，目标不是知识而是发现。勘探在找到资源时结束，而不是在地图画完时结束。

senses.title: Reconnaissance
senses.titleCN: 侦察：先派一小队去看路
senses.definition: a preliminary examination of an area or situation, especially for military purposes
senses.definitionCN: 对地区或情况的初步查看，尤指军事目的
senses.example: A patrol carried out an exploration of the valley before the advance.
senses.exampleCN: 推进之前，一支巡逻队对山谷进行了侦察。
senses.why: Exploration can be a small, cautious move made before a larger one. The information gathered is meant to guide action, not to satisfy curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 探索可以是在大行动之前的小心试探。收集的信息是为了指导行动，而不是满足好奇。

senses.title: Data exploration
senses.titleCN: 数据探索：先看分布再建模型
senses.definition: the preliminary examination of a dataset to find patterns, anomalies, and structure
senses.definitionCN: 对数据集进行初步考察，以发现模式、异常与结构
senses.example: Data exploration revealed a cluster nobody had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 数据探索揭示了一个没人预料到的聚类。
senses.why: Statistics borrowed the word for looking before formal testing: the analyst moves through the data without a fixed hypothesis, letting structure appear.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用这个词来表示‘正式检验之前的查看’：分析者不带固定假设地在数据中移动，让结构自己显现。

senses.title: Artistic or intellectual exploration
senses.titleCN: 艺术与思想探索：不预设结论地试
senses.definition: the open-ended testing of forms, ideas, or materials without a fixed outcome
senses.definitionCN: 对形式、观念或材料进行无固定结果的开放尝试
senses.example: The album is an exploration of silence as a musical material.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑把静默当作音乐材料进行探索。
senses.why: The final sense removes the map entirely: the work is the record of a search whose destination was not known in advance.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个义项完全去掉地图：作品就是一次搜索的记录，而终点事先并不知晓。

intro.en: Exploration is from Latin exploratio, from explorare, to investigate. The deeper link to plorare, to cry out, is a hunting hypothesis and should be marked as uncertain.
intro.cn: exploration 来自拉丁 exploratio，源头 explorare‘调查’。更深层与 plorare‘呼喊’的联系是一种狩猎假说，应标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: To investigate, examine, or search out. The verb is attested, but its internal analysis is disputed: it may contain ex- plus a root related to calling or crying out.
items.cn: 调查、检查、搜寻。该动词有文献可证，但其内部结构有争议：可能含 ex- 加一个与‘呼喊’有关的词根。

items.en: To cry out or wail. Some sources connect explorare with the shouts of hunters flushing game; others reject the link. Treat the hunting image as a plausible reconstruction, not a fact.
items.cn: 呼喊、哭喊。一些来源把 explorare 联系到猎人把猎物惊起时的喊声；另一些否认。应把狩猎意象视为合理重构，而非事实。

items.en: An investigation or a searching out. In military writing it could mean reconnaissance, the small move made before a large one.
items.cn: 调查或搜寻。在军事文献中可指侦察，即大行动之前的小动作。

items.en: French passed the noun to English. The geographical sense travelled with the age of voyages.
items.cn: 法语把名词传给英语。地理义随航海时代一起来。

items.en: English exploration appears in the 16c, the century of ocean voyages. It first described travel to regions absent from European maps.
items.cn: 英语 exploration 在 16 世纪出现，那是远洋航行的世纪。它最初描述前往欧洲地图上没有的地区。

items.en: The 19c-20c extended exploration to science, medicine, statistics, and art. Each field keeps the same condition: the territory is unknown before the move.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，exploration 扩展到科学、医学、统计与艺术。每个领域都保留同一条件：在行动之前，领域是未知的。

note.en: The first group is the explore family; the second compares journeys or inquiries into the unknown, each with a different aim.
note.cn: 第一组是 explore 词族；第二组比较进入未知的旅程或探究，各自目标不同。

entries.definition: to travel through or investigate an unknown area. It is the action behind exploration.
entries.definitionCN: 穿越或调查未知区域；是 exploration 背后的动作。

entries.definition: a person who explores. The word carries a history of voyages and claims.
entries.definitionCN: 探索者；探险家；带有一段航行与声索的历史。

entries.definition: done in order to find out something. It describes the purpose of a study or procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 为查明某事而做的；描述研究或程序的目的。

entries.definition: not yet examined or travelled through. It names the territory before exploration.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未被考察或穿越的；命名探索之前的领域。

entries.definition: an organized journey with a particular purpose. It is a single mission, while exploration can be the whole activity.
entries.definitionCN: 有特定目的的组织化旅程；是单次任务，而 exploration 可以是整体活动。

entries.definition: a systematic inquiry into facts, often official. It usually has a question to answer, not a blank map.
entries.definitionCN: 对事实的系统调查，常为官方性的；通常有明确问题，而不是空白地图。

entries.definition: a detailed examination of an area or a group. It is more structured and less open-ended than exploration.
entries.definitionCN: 对地区或群体的详细考察；比 exploration 更有结构、更少开放性。

entries.definition: a preliminary examination of an area for military purposes. It is exploration reduced to information for action.
entries.definitionCN: 为军事目的对地区进行的初步查看；是压缩成‘行动信息’的 exploration。

entries.definition: an attempt to find something specific. It assumes the object is known; exploration assumes it is not.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找特定目标；预设目标已知，而 exploration 预设目标未知。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ex- out plus explorare, to search out. The hunting-cry link to plorare is a plausible reconstruction and is marked as uncertain.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ex-‘向外’加 explorare‘搜寻’。与 plorare‘呼喊’的狩猎联系是合理重构，标为来源不确定。

normal.en: Ex- out, explorare search out: exploration is searching outward.
normal.cn: ex- 向外，explorare 搜寻：exploration 就是向外搜寻。

normal.en: A torch in a cave is the simplest picture of exploration.
normal.cn: 洞穴里的一束手电光，就是 exploration 最简单的画面。

normal.en: Space exploration sends a machine where a person cannot yet go.
normal.cn: 太空探索把人还不能去的地方交给机器。

normal.en: Surgical exploration looks inside because imaging has stopped answering.
normal.cn: 医学探查往里面看，是因为影像已经回答不了。

normal.en: Data exploration looks before it tests.
normal.cn: 数据探索先看，再检验。

abstract.en: Exploration is defined by the absence of a map, not by distance.
abstract.cn: 探索由‘没有地图’定义，而不是由距离定义。

abstract.en: Every exploration produces a map, and every map quietly ends the exploration it records.
abstract.cn: 每次探索都产出一张地图，而每张地图都在悄悄结束它所记录的那次探索。

abstract.en: Somebody always pays for the blank space on the map, and it is rarely the one drawing it.
abstract.cn: 地图上的空白总要有人付出代价，而付代价的很少是画图的人。

examples.en: The exploration of the cave system revealed a river no map had shown.
examples.cn: 对洞穴系统的探索发现了一条地图上没有的河。

examples.en: Her exploration of the topic began with a single footnote.
examples.cn: 她对这个课题的探究始自一条脚注。

examples.en: The company halted exploration when the price of oil fell.
examples.cn: 油价下跌后，公司停止了勘探。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一克死，泼了泪神”——探索到绝境，一克希望死了，泪水泼向神：exploration 探索、勘探。

root: 源自拉丁 explorare（调查、搜寻）与 exploratio；更深的 plorare‘呼喊’联系属狩猎假说，来源不确定。核心是“在没有地图的地方向外搜寻”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of exploration, one condition: the territory is unknown before the move. The territory may be a continent, an archive, a planet, an abdomen, a rock layer, an enemy valley, a dataset, or a medium.
sensesIntro.cn: exploration 的八个义项共有一个条件：行动之前领域未知。领域可以是大陆、档案、行星、腹腔、岩层、敌方山谷、数据集或某种媒介。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a torch beam moving through a dark cave, beyond it an unmapped blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：手电光在黑暗洞穴中移动，光圈之外是未画地图的空白。

chain: ENGLISH EXPLORATION TRAVEL INTO THE UNKNOWN
THE MOVEMENT ITSELF MAKES THE MAP

branches.en: GEOGRAPHICAL AND INTELLECTUAL TERRAIN: a river and an archive are both entered without a complete account.
branches.cn: 地理与智识地形：河流与档案都是在没有完整记录时进入的。

branches.en: DISTANT AND SUBSURFACE UNKNOWN: space and oil lie beyond ordinary reach, so instruments lead.
branches.cn: 远方与地下的未知：太空与石油超出日常触及，因此由仪器带路。

branches.en: THE BODY'S INTERIOR: surgery explores when imaging can no longer answer.
branches.cn: 身体内部：影像无法回答时，手术去探查。

branches.en: THE SMALL MOVE BEFORE THE LARGE: reconnaissance gathers information for action.
branches.cn: 大行动前的小动作：侦察为行动收集信息。

branches.en: THE OPEN SEARCH: data and art are explored without a fixed hypothesis or destination.
branches.cn: 开放式搜寻：数据与艺术在没有固定假设或终点的情况下被探索。

intro.en: Exploration is explor- plus -ation. The family includes explore, explorer, exploratory, explorative, and unexplored. Note that exploit is not from explorare; it comes through explicare, to unfold.
intro.cn: exploration 是 explor- 加 -ation。词族包括 explore、explorer、exploratory、explorative 与 unexplored。注意 exploit 不来自 explorare，而经 explicare‘展开’而来。

latinIntro.en: The attested forms are explorare and exploratio. The link to plorare, to cry out, is a reconstruction from hunting practice and is marked as uncertain, not proven.
latinIntro.cn: 可证形式是 explorare 与 exploratio。与 plorare‘呼喊’的联系是从狩猎实践做出的重构，标为来源不确定，而非已证。

items.meaning: to travel through or investigate the unknown
items.example: They explored the valley for two days.
items.exampleCN: 他们用了两天探索这个山谷。

items.example: The exploration found no trace of the camp.
items.exampleCN: 这次探索没有发现营地的痕迹。

items.meaning: done in order to find out
items.example: They ran an exploratory analysis first.
items.exampleCN: 他们先做了一项探索性分析。

items.example: The explorer kept a careful journal.
items.exampleCN: 探险家仔细记了日志。

items.example: The ridge remains unexplored.
items.exampleCN: 那道山脊仍未被人探索。

items.example: The study is explorative rather than confirmatory.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究是探索性的，而非确认性的。

items.example: The sample was tested exploratorily.
items.exampleCN: 样本被以探索方式测试。

items.example: The agency set an explorational target.
items.exampleCN: 该机构设定了一个勘探目标。

items.structure: Old French esploit < Latin explicare (unfold); not from explorare
items.meaning: to use a resource, often unfairly
items.meaningCN: 开发利用；剥削（经 explicare‘展开’，与 explorare 不同源）
items.example: The company exploited the mineral deposit.
items.exampleCN: 公司开发了这处矿床。

items.meaning: the use or unfair use of a resource or person
items.meaningCN: 开发利用；剥削（与 exploration 不同源，需区分）
items.example: The report documented labour exploitation.
items.exampleCN: 报告记录了劳工剥削。

latinEntries.meaning: to cry out, wail; possibly the source of explorare
latinEntries.meaningCN: 呼喊；哭喊（与 explorare 的联系属重构，来源不确定）

definition_zh: 海洋生物多样性；海洋物种多样性；海洋遗传多样性；海洋生态系统多样性
definition_en: the variety of life in the sea, from genes and species to habitats and ecosystems
core_image: 珊瑚礁、深海平原与海草床在同一片蓝色里并存，每一处都挤满不同的生物
scene: 潜水员在珊瑚礁上记录鱼群，每一种新出现的颜色都被写进水下记录板。 Coral reefs hold a large share of marine biodiversity despite covering a tiny part of the sea floor.
sceneCN: 这里指「海洋中生命形式的整体多样性」（第 1 个义项：从基因、物种到生境与生态系统的海洋生命差异总量）；句意为珊瑚礁虽然只覆盖海底极小一部分，却拥有很大比例的海洋生物多样性。场景物件：珊瑚、鱼群、水下记录板、海草。

pos.zh: 海洋生物多样性（不可数；指多套系统时偶用复数 marine biodiversities）

collocations.zh: 海洋生物多样性的测量
气候变化下的海洋生物多样性

forms.label: 相关形容词（生物多样的）
同义学术说法（海洋生物多样性）
定语形式（海洋生物多样性的）

senses.title: The total variety of sea life
senses.definition: the variety of life in the sea, from genes and species to habitats and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 海洋中从基因、物种到生境与生态系统的生命差异总量
senses.example: Coral reefs hold a large share of marine biodiversity despite covering a tiny part of the sea floor.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁虽然只覆盖海底极小一部分，却拥有很大比例的海洋生物多样性。
senses.why: Marine locates the variety in salt water and biodiversity names variety itself, so the phrase is the whole range of sea life taken as one quantity.
senses.whyCN: marine 把多样性定位到咸水，biodiversity 指多样性本身，因此这个短语是把全部海洋生命当作一个总量。

senses.title: Species richness
senses.definition: the number of marine species present in a place or in the ocean as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 某一海域或整个海洋中出现的海洋物种数量
senses.example: The survey found unexpectedly high marine biodiversity on the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 调查在陆坡发现了异常高的海洋生物多样性。
senses.why: Counting species is the oldest way to measure variety, so the phrase often narrows to species richness.
senses.whyCN: 统计物种是衡量多样性最古老的方法，因此这个短语常收窄到物种丰富度。

senses.title: Genetic variation in the sea
senses.definition: the genetic differences among individuals and populations of marine organisms
senses.definitionCN: 海洋生物个体与种群之间的遗传差异
senses.example: Marine biodiversity below the species level buffers populations against warming.
senses.exampleCN: 物种层面以下的海洋生物多样性为种群抵御变暖提供缓冲。
senses.why: Variety exists inside a species too, and molecular tools made that layer visible, so the phrase extends downward to genes.
senses.whyCN: 多样性也存在于物种内部，分子工具让这一层可见，于是这个短语向下延伸到基因。

senses.title: Habitat and ecosystem diversity
senses.titleCN: 海洋生境与生态系统多样性
senses.definition: the range of marine habitat types, such as reefs, seagrass beds, vents and abyssal plains
senses.definitionCN: 海洋生境类型的范围，如珊瑚礁、海草床、热液喷口与深海平原
senses.example: Marine biodiversity depends on having many kinds of habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物多样性依赖于拥有多种生境。
senses.why: Ecologists count variety at the scale of ecosystems as well, so the phrase can mean the diversity of habitats rather than of species.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家也在生态系统尺度上统计多样性，因此这个短语也可指生境多样性而非物种多样性。

senses.title: Concentration in hotspots
senses.definition: the unusually dense variety found in coral reefs, estuaries and deep-sea vents
senses.definitionCN: 珊瑚礁、河口与深海热液喷口等处异常密集的多样性
senses.example: The reef is a hotspot of marine biodiversity in an otherwise empty sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这片礁在原本空阔的海中是一处海洋生物多样性热点。
senses.why: Conservation needs priorities, so the phrase came to name places where variety is concentrated rather than evenly spread.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要优先级，因此这个短语开始指多样性集中而非均匀分布的地方。

senses.title: The resource base of fisheries
senses.definition: the variety of marine life on which capture fisheries and aquaculture depend
senses.definitionCN: 捕捞渔业与水产养殖所依赖的海洋生命多样性
senses.example: Declining marine biodiversity makes catches less stable.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物多样性下降使渔获更不稳定。
senses.why: Fisheries see variety as portfolio insurance, so the phrase acquired an economic reading alongside the ecological one.
senses.whyCN: 渔业把多样性看作组合保险，因此这个短语在生态读法之外多了经济读法。

senses.title: A conservation policy target
senses.definition: the stated goal of protecting a share of marine variety in treaties and national plans
senses.definitionCN: 条约与国家规划中保护一定比例海洋多样性的既定目标
senses.example: The agreement sets a marine biodiversity target for protected areas.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议为保护区设定了海洋生物多样性目标。
senses.why: Once governments promised to protect variety, the phrase became a measurable policy target.
senses.whyCN: 当政府承诺保护多样性，这个短语就成了可测量的政策目标。

senses.title: A measured index
senses.definition: a numeric score, such as a diversity index, used to compare marine sites
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较不同海域的数值评分，如多样性指数
senses.example: The team calculated marine biodiversity for each station.
senses.exampleCN: 团队为每个站点计算了海洋生物多样性。
senses.why: Management requires numbers, so the concept was operationalized into indices and scores.
senses.whyCN: 管理需要数字，于是这个概念被操作化为指数与评分。

intro.en: Marine biodiversity joins Latin marinus 'of the sea' to a twentieth-century coinage that combines Greek bios 'life' with Latin diversus 'turned different ways'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marine biodiversity 把拉丁 marinus「海的」与一个二十世纪新造词并置，后者把希腊 bios「生命」与拉丁 diversus「转向不同方向」组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mare 'sea' gave the adjective marinus 'of the sea', which English borrowed as marine; the deeper origin of mare is uncertain.
items.cn: mare「海」形成形容词 marinus「海的」，英语借入为 marine；mare 的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Greek bios meant 'life, way of life' and entered modern science through the combining form bio-.
items.cn: 希腊 bios 意为「生命、生活方式」，经组合形式 bio- 进入现代科学。

items.en: Diversus, the past participle of divertere 'to turn in different directions', gave English diverse and diversity.
items.cn: diversus 是 divertere「转向不同方向」的过去分词，衍生英语 diverse 与 diversity。

items.en: Biodiversity is generally dated to the mid 1980s and widely attributed to Walter G. Rosen; it spread after a 1988 symposium volume edited by E. O. Wilson.
items.cn: biodiversity 一般认为是二十世纪八十年代中期所造，广泛归功于 Walter G. Rosen；它在 1988 年由 E. O. Wilson 主编的会议文集后流行。

items.en: Marine was attached to the new noun once ocean scientists needed to separate sea variety from the general term.
items.cn: 当海洋科学家需要把海洋多样性从通用词中分出，marine 便被加到这个新名词前。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of mare is unknown, the pre-Greek source of bios is uncertain, and the first use of the exact English phrase is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：mare 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，bios 的前希腊语来源不确定，确切英语短语的最早使用没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds the words built on the same bio- and diversity stock; group two holds neighbouring marine variety concepts and measures.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 bio- 与 diversity 词干的词；第二组是邻近的海洋多样性概念与测量词。

entries.definition: The variety of life on land or in water; marine biodiversity restricts it to the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 陆地或水中生命的多样性；marine biodiversity 把它限定到海洋。

entries.definition: Relating to the sea; it only says where the variety is found, not that variety exists.
entries.definitionCN: 与海有关的；它只说多样性在哪里，并不表示多样性本身。

entries.definition: Describing a place rich in variety; it cannot serve as the name of the measured concept.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某地多样性丰富；它不能作为被测量概念的名称。

entries.definition: The science of marine organisms; marine biodiversity is what that science studies.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋生物的科学；海洋生物多样性是它研究的对象。

entries.definition: The count of species in a place; it is one measurable part of marine biodiversity, not the whole concept.
entries.definitionCN: 某地物种的数量；它是海洋生物多样性可测的一部分，而不是整个概念。

entries.definition: The variety of ecosystem types; in the sea it is the habitat layer of marine biodiversity.
entries.definitionCN: 生态系统类型的多样性；在海洋中它是海洋生物多样性的生境层。

entries.definition: Variation among genes and populations; it is the layer below species in marine biodiversity.
entries.definitionCN: 基因与种群之间的变异；它是海洋生物多样性中物种以下的一层。

entries.definition: The longer wording for the same idea; marine biological diversity is the formal variant of this phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念的较长说法；海洋生物多样性是这一短语的正式变体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek and Latin parts, real ecological layers and real policy collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁构件、真实生态层次与真实政策搭配。

normal.en: Bio- is life, diversity is difference, so biodiversity is life's difference.
normal.cn: bio- 是生命，diversity 是差异，生物多样性就是生命的差异。

normal.en: Marine comes from Latin mare, the sea.
normal.cn: marine 出自拉丁 mare，即海。

normal.en: The concept has three layers: genes, species and ecosystems.
normal.cn: 这个概念有三层：基因、物种与生态系统。

normal.en: Coral reefs are hotspots out of all proportion to their area.
normal.cn: 珊瑚礁的面积很小，却是极不成比例的热点。

normal.en: Fisheries treat variety as a portfolio that spreads risk.
normal.cn: 渔业把多样性看作分散风险的组合。

abstract.en: Picture a blue library whose books are genes, species and habitats.
abstract.cn: 想象一座蓝色图书馆，书是基因、物种与生境。

abstract.en: Picture a reef as a crowded city and the open sea as empty countryside.
abstract.cn: 想象珊瑚礁是拥挤的城市，外海是空旷的乡野。

abstract.en: Picture a net made of many species; lose strands and the whole net weakens.
abstract.cn: 想象一张由许多物种编成的网，抽掉几股，整张网就变弱。

examples.en: Marine biodiversity is highest where habitats overlap.
examples.cn: 海洋生物多样性在生境交叠处最高。

examples.en: The treaty asks nations to report on marine biodiversity.
examples.cn: 该条约要求各国报告海洋生物多样性状况。

examples.en: Deep-sea mining could reduce marine biodiversity before it is even described.
examples.cn: 深海采矿可能在海洋生物多样性尚未被描述之前就把它削减。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marine（海洋的）+ biodiversity（生物多样性）」——海里的生命差异总量 → 海洋生物多样性

root: 拉丁 mare「海」（更深来源不确定）→ marinus「海的」→ 英语 marine；希腊 bios「生命」+ 拉丁 diversus「转向不同方向」→ diversity；biodiversity 为二十世纪八十年代新造词，一般归功于 Walter G. Rosen。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one range of sea life: total variety, species count, genetic variation, habitat range, hotspots, fisheries base, policy target and measured index.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一片海洋生命范围展开：总多样性、物种数、遗传变异、生境范围、热点、渔业基础、政策目标与测量指数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reef, seagrass bed and open blue water side by side, each crowded with different forms of life.
core.cn: 核心意象：珊瑚礁、海草床与开阔蓝水并排，每一处都挤满不同的生命形态。

branches.en: CONCEPT TO NUMBER: a broad idea becomes a diversity index that can be compared across stations.
branches.cn: 从概念到数字：宽泛的观念变成可在站点间比较的多样性指数。

branches.en: SPECIES TO FISHERIES: the number of species underpins the stability of catches.
branches.cn: 从物种到渔业：物种数量支撑渔获的稳定。

branches.en: GENES AND HABITATS: variation inside species and between habitats both supply resilience.
branches.cn: 基因与生境：种内变异与生境差异都提供韧性。

branches.en: THE HOTSPOTS: variety concentrates in a few places that stand out.
branches.cn: 热点区：多样性集中在格外突出的少数海域。

branches.en: THE TARGET: what fisheries depend on becomes what governments promise to protect.
branches.cn: 政策目标：渔业赖以生存的东西，成为政府承诺保护的对象。

intro.en: Marine biodiversity is a hybrid compound: a Latin adjective plus a modern noun made of a Greek prefix and a Latin root. Both halves are transparent.
intro.cn: marine biodiversity 是混合复合词：一个拉丁形容词，加一个由希腊前缀与拉丁词根构成的现代名词。两半都透明。

latinIntro.en: Mare supplies marine; diversus supplies diversity; Greek bios supplies the bio- element. The phrase mixes both classical layers.
latinIntro.cn: mare 提供 marine；diversus 提供 diversity；希腊 bios 提供 bio- 成分。这个短语混合了两个古典层。

items.structure: Latin marinus 'of the sea' from mare
items.example: Marine animals range from plankton to whales.
items.exampleCN: 海洋动物从浮游生物到鲸都有。

items.example: Bio- appears in biology and biosphere.
items.exampleCN: bio- 出现在生物学与生物圈等词中。

items.example: Diversity rises toward the tropics.
items.exampleCN: 多样性向热带升高。

items.example: Biodiversity is measured at three levels.
items.exampleCN: 生物多样性在三个层面测量。

items.example: Marine biodiversity is unevenly distributed.
items.exampleCN: 海洋生物多样性分布不均。

items.example: The reef is extremely biodiverse.
items.exampleCN: 这片礁的生命形式极为丰富。

items.meaning: the count or abundance of a category
items.meaningCN: 某一类别的数量或丰富程度
items.example: Species richness is one metric.
items.exampleCN: 物种丰富度是一项指标。

items.meaning: a place of concentrated activity or variety
items.meaningCN: 活动或多样性集中的地点
items.example: The reef is a biodiversity hotspot.
items.exampleCN: 这片礁是生物多样性热点。

items.meaning: the state of being found only in one place
items.example: High endemism raises the value of the hotspot.
items.exampleCN: 高度的特有性提高了热点价值。

latinEntries.structure: diversus, diversa, diversum (adjective; participle of divertere)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 转向不同方向的；多样的

definition_zh: 城市开发；城市发展；城市建设项目；城市更新；可持续城市发展
definition_en: the building, expansion and improvement of land and services within a city
core_image: 围挡上印着未来的公园与地铁线，围挡里面是刚挖开的土坑和几台静立的挖机
scene: 河岸边旧仓库被推倒，新楼盘的围挡上印着公园与地铁的规划图。 Urban development reshaped the old harbour district.
sceneCN: 这里 urban development 指「城市土地与设施的建设与改造」（第 1 个义项：城市空间的实体开发）；句意为城市开发重塑了这片旧港区。可辨识物件：围挡、规划图、挖机、旧仓库。

pos.zh: 城市开发；城市发展（通常不可数，指多个项目时可说 urban developments）

derivatives.zh: 基础动词 develop 去掉 -ment 后的形式，由「逐步展开」偏移为「使土地或地区具备用途」
develop + -ment（名词后缀）→ 偏移为「逐步展开的过程与成果」
develop + -er（施事后缀）→ 偏移为「做开发的人或公司」
development + -al（形容词后缀）→ 偏移为「与发育或发展相关的」
re-（再）+ development → 偏移为「对已开发地段的再次改造」
under-（不足）+ development → 偏移为「发展不足的状态」
urban + -ize（动词后缀）→ 偏移为「使某地转为城市形态」

senses.title: Physical building of city land
senses.definition: the construction of buildings, roads and services on land within or next to a city
senses.definitionCN: 在城市之内或紧邻城市的土地上修建建筑、道路与服务设施
senses.example: Urban development reshaped the old harbour district.
senses.exampleCN: 城市开发重塑了这片旧港区。
senses.why: development means the gradual unfolding of something, and applied to land it means bringing a site into use step by step.
senses.whyCN: development 指某物逐步展开，用在土地上就是让一块地一步步具备用途。

senses.title: City planning of growth
senses.titleCN: 对城市增长所作的规划
senses.definition: the planned direction of a city's growth, including zoning and phasing
senses.definitionCN: 对城市增长方向所做的计划，包括分区与分期
senses.example: The urban development map reserved the flood plain as parkland.
senses.exampleCN: 城市开发图把洪泛区留作公园用地。
senses.why: once growth can be steered, development stops describing what happened and starts naming what is intended.
senses.whyCN: 一旦增长可以被引导，开发就不再描述已发生的事，而开始命名所意图的事。

senses.title: A specific development project
senses.definition: one scheme, such as a housing estate or a commercial block, built as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个整体来建的一项工程，如住宅区或商业街区
senses.example: Three urban developments line the new tram route.
senses.exampleCN: 三个城市开发项目沿新电车线路排开。
senses.why: the uncountable process is countable when it is packaged as a project, which is why the plural exists.
senses.whyCN: 这一不可数的过程在被打包成工程时就可数了，因此才有复数形式。

senses.title: Economic growth of a city
senses.titleCN: 城市的经济增长与发展
senses.definition: the growth of a city's economy, jobs and tax base
senses.definitionCN: 城市经济、就业与税基的增长
senses.example: Urban development brought warehouses but few skilled jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 城市发展带来了仓库，却几乎没有带来技术岗位。
senses.why: development also measures a place's economic advance, so the same phrase serves planners and economists.
senses.whyCN: 开发也衡量一个地方的经济进展，因此同一短语同时供规划者与经济学家使用。

senses.title: Urban renewal
senses.definition: the replacement or repair of decayed districts rather than the extension of new ones
senses.definitionCN: 对衰败城区的替换或修缮，而非向外扩建新区
senses.example: Urban development here means knocking down and rebuilding, not expanding.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的城市开发指的是拆掉重建，而不是向外扩张。
senses.why: when a city has no empty land, development must reuse what already exists.
senses.whyCN: 当城市没有空地，开发只能重新利用已有的东西。

senses.title: Real estate development
senses.definition: the commercial building of housing and offices for sale or rent
senses.definitionCN: 为出售或出租而商业性建造住房与写字楼
senses.example: Private urban development outpaced the public water network.
senses.exampleCN: 私人房地产开发跑在了公共水管网前面。
senses.why: the phrase is neutral, so it covers both public works and the private property business.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是中性的，因此既覆盖公共工程，也覆盖私人房地产业。

senses.title: Sustainable urban development
senses.definition: growth planned so that transport, housing and green space remain workable long term
senses.definitionCN: 为使交通、住房与绿地在长期内仍可运作而规划的增长
senses.example: Sustainable urban development means building where the drains already run.
senses.exampleCN: 可持续城市发展意味着在排水系统已经到位的地方建设。
senses.why: the phrase acquired a policy sense once the costs of unplanned growth became visible.
senses.whyCN: 当无序增长的代价显现，这个短语就获得了一个政策义。

senses.title: Institutions and policy
senses.titleCN: 城市发展的制度与政策
senses.definition: the laws, agencies and financing through which building is approved and paid for
senses.definitionCN: 批准并资助建设的法律、机构与融资安排
senses.example: Urban development is decided in offices far from the sites.
senses.exampleCN: 城市发展是在远离工地的办公室里被决定的。
senses.why: what gets built is settled by permits and budgets, so the phrase extends to the machinery behind the building.
senses.whyCN: 建什么由许可与预算决定，因此这个短语扩展到建筑背后的那套机器。

intro.en: Urban development joins urban, from Latin urbs 'city', to development, whose deeper origin is uncertain; the phrase is a twentieth-century planning term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: urban development 把来自拉丁 urbs「城市」的 urban 与 development 组合起来，后者更早的来源不确定；这个短语是二十世纪的规划术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Urbanus 'of the city' came from urbs 'city', whose origin before Latin is not established.
items.cn: urbanus「城市的」来自 urbs「城市」，而 urbs 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Old French desveloper meant 'to unwrap, to unfold'. The sense of gradual growth came later, in English.
items.cn: 古法语 desveloper 意为「解开、展开」，逐步成长的意思后来才在英语中出现。

items.en: English develop first meant to unfold or bring out what was latent, then to build up land and resources.
items.cn: 英语 develop 先指展开或引出潜在之物，后指开发土地与资源。

items.en: The noun development took the sense of a built result as well as a process, which is why a site can be called a development.
items.cn: 名词 development 兼指过程与建成的结果，因此一块地也可以被称为一项开发。

items.en: Urban development became a standard phrase in post-war planning, housing and international aid writing.
items.cn: urban development 在战后规划、住房与国际援助文献中成为标准说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of desveloper is unsettled and the exact first use of the phrase is unrecorded; any earlier form proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：desveloper 的更早来源无定论，这个短语的确切首见也没有记录；为它提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates the compound from the overlapping planning terms; group two holds the physical and social processes it is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组把这一复合词与重叠的规划术语分开；第二组是常与它混淆的实体与社会过程。

entries.definition: The professional activity of deciding land use and layout; development is the building that follows the plan.
entries.definitionCN: 决定土地使用与布局的专业活动；开发是跟着规划进行的建设。

entries.definition: The increase in a city's size or population; growth can be measured, while development includes deliberate improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 城市规模或人口的增长；增长可以测量，而开发还包含有意的改良。

entries.definition: Development of land that was already built on; it is one branch of urban development, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 对已建成土地的再次开发；它是城市开发的一个分支，而非全部。

entries.definition: The general process of growth or building; adding urban narrows it to cities but does not change its logic.
entries.definitionCN: 增长或建设的一般过程；加上 urban 只是把它收窄到城市，并不改变其逻辑。

entries.definition: Low-density outward spread; it is a pattern that development can produce, and usually a criticism of it.
entries.definitionCN: 低密度的向外铺开；它是开发可能产生的一种形态，通常带着批评。

entries.definition: The activity of building; it is the physical work, while development covers financing, approval and use.
entries.definitionCN: 建造的活动；它是实体施工，而开发还涵盖融资、审批与用途。

entries.definition: Roads, pipes and power that support a city; infrastructure is one input to development, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑城市的道路、管网与电力；基础设施是开发的投入之一，不是同义词。

entries.definition: The renewal of a poor district that displaces its poorer residents; it is one social outcome of development.
entries.definitionCN: 贫困街区被翻新、却把较穷的居民挤走；它是开发的一种社会后果。

entries.definition: Adoption of modern methods and institutions; it can happen without any building, so it is broader than development.
entries.definitionCN: 采纳现代方法与制度；它可以在完全不建设的情况下发生，因此比开发更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves, the real planning phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的部分、真实的规划说法与真实同族词。

normal.en: urban 'of the city' + development 'unfolding': the city unfolded into use.
normal.cn: urban「城市的」+ development「展开」：城市被一步步展开到可用状态。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: urban development project, urban development plan, urban development policy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：城市开发项目、城市开发规划、城市发展政策。

normal.en: The family runs develop, development, developer, developmental, redevelopment, underdevelopment.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 develop、development、developer、developmental、redevelopment、underdevelopment。

normal.en: A site is called a development because the noun names the built result as well as the process.
normal.cn: 一块地被称为一项开发，是因为这个名词兼指过程与建成的结果。

normal.en: Sustainable urban development adds the condition that drains, transport and green space must keep working.
normal.cn: 可持续城市发展加上了排水、交通与绿地必须持续可用的条件。

abstract.en: Picture a fence painted with the park that will stand behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道围挡，上面画着将来会立在它后面的公园。

abstract.en: Picture an old warehouse whose bricks are numbered for reuse before it is pulled down.
abstract.cn: 想象一座旧仓库在被推倒之前，砖块已被编号准备再用。

abstract.en: Picture a permit signed far away that decides which field will become a street.
abstract.cn: 想象一份在很远的地方签下的许可，决定了哪片田会变成街道。

examples.en: Urban development stalled when the water supply could not keep pace.
examples.cn: 供水跟不上时，城市开发停滞了。

examples.en: The report treats urban development as a public health issue.
examples.cn: 这份报告把城市发展当作公共卫生问题来处理。

examples.en: New urban developments must leave room for drainage.
examples.cn: 新的城市开发项目必须留出排水空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「urban（城市的）+ development（展开、发展）」——把城市一步步展开建起来 → 城市开发

root: urban（拉丁 urbs「城市」→ urbanus「城市的」）+ development（古法语 desveloper「解开、展开」，更早来源不确定）；短语为二十世纪规划用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: land is brought into use, and the same act is then seen as a plan, a project, an economy, a renewal, a property business, a sustainability condition and finally as the offices that permit it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：土地被带人可使用状态，这个动作随后被看作规划、项目、经济、更新、房地产业、可持续条件，最后被看作批准它的那些办公室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a site fenced off from its old use and opened toward a new one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块地从旧用途中被围起来，朝一个新用途打开。

branches.en: FROM GROUND TO PROJECT: physical work on a site, then the same work packaged and counted as one scheme.
branches.cn: 从地面到项目：工地上的实体施工，再把同一施工打包计作一项工程。

branches.en: STEERING GROWTH: the plan comes before the building and decides its direction.
branches.cn: 引导增长：规划先于建设，并决定其方向。

branches.en: MONEY AND JOBS: development is also an economic and property process with its own measures.
branches.cn: 钱与岗位：开发也是一种经济与房地产过程，有自己的衡量方式。

branches.en: REBUILDING WHAT EXISTS: when there is no empty land, development must reuse the old district.
branches.cn: 重建已有之物：没有空地时，开发只能重新利用旧城区。

branches.en: CONDITIONS AND PERMISSIONS: sustainability sets limits, and offices and budgets decide what is allowed.
branches.cn: 条件与许可：可持续性设定限制，办公室与预算决定什么被允许。

intro.en: The phrase is two words, and each contributes a productive family: urban for place, development for unfolding.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个词组成，每个都贡献一个高产词族：urban 表地点，development 表展开。

latinIntro.en: Urban is Latin-derived, from urbs; development is not Latin at all, coming through Old French with an uncertain deeper origin.
latinIntro.cn: urban 源自拉丁 urbs；development 并非拉丁词，经古法语进入英语，更早来源不确定。

items.example: The stem supplies the place half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供短语中表地点的那一半。

items.example: Urban land carries a different price.
items.exampleCN: 城市土地的价格不同。

items.example: The site developed over twenty years.
items.exampleCN: 这块地在二十年间逐步开发。

items.example: The suffix makes a noun of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成名词。

items.example: The developer missed the drainage deadline.
items.exampleCN: 开发商错过了排水工程的期限。

items.example: The project entered its developmental stage.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目进入开发阶段。

items.example: Redevelopment repeats the work on old ground.
items.exampleCN: 再开发是在旧地面上重做一遍。

items.example: Underdevelopment marks a shortfall, not a stage.
items.exampleCN: 发展不足标记的是欠缺，而不是某个阶段。

items.example: The road urbanized the valley within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这条路在十年内使山谷城市化了。

definition_zh: 坚持不懈；毅力；持续存在；固执；数据的持久性；病原体的持续存在；环境残留的持久性；视觉暂留；长期存续
definition_en: the quality of continuing firmly despite difficulty, the state of something continuing to exist or remain, or a technical property such as stored data surviving or a substance remaining in the environment
core_image: 一只手一直按在同一颗按钮上，那盏灯始终没有灭
scene: 同一道题她算了三遍，草稿纸翻到背面还在写，最后终于算对。 Her persistence paid off when the third attempt came out right.
sceneCN: 这里 persistence 是「坚持不懈」（第 1 个义项：面对困难仍持续用力、不放弃的品质）；句意：第三遍终于算对，她的坚持不懈有了回报。

pos.zh: 坚持不懈；毅力；持续存在；持久性；固执

derivatives.zh: 坚持不懈的；持续的；顽固的

senses.title: Continuing against difficulty
senses.definition: the quality of continuing firmly with an aim despite obstacles, discouragement, or repeated failure
senses.definitionCN: 面对障碍、打击或反复失败仍坚定继续追求目标的品质
senses.example: Her persistence in asking questions finally got an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚持追问，最终得到了答案。
senses.why: Latin persistere is per- 'thoroughly' plus sistere 'to stand'. Persistence is standing your ground completely: the hand stays on the button while the light is still off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 persistere 是 per-“彻底”加 sistere“站立”。persistence 就是彻底站住脚：灯还没亮，手也不离开按钮。

senses.title: The state of continuing to exist
senses.definition: the fact of something continuing to exist or occur over time, without disappearing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物随时间继续存在或发生、并未消失的事实
senses.example: The persistence of the tradition surprised the researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 这一传统延续至今，让研究者感到意外。
senses.why: Nothing is pushing back here; the thing simply fails to stop. The same standing image is used without the struggle, and persistence becomes duration.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有任何阻力，事物只是没有停下来。同一个“站住”的意象去掉了挣扎，persistence 于是变成了持续。

senses.title: Holding to an idea too long
senses.definition: the tendency to keep repeating or defending an idea, request, or belief after it should have been dropped
senses.definitionCN: 在某个想法、请求或信念本应放弃之后仍反复重复或辩护的倾向
senses.example: His persistence about the missing file began to annoy the office.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了地追问那份丢失的文件，让办公室的人开始厌烦。
senses.why: Standing too long in one place turns virtue into obstacle. This sense keeps the posture but withdraws the approval: the hand is still on the button, and now nobody wants the light.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个地方站得太久，美德就变成障碍。这个义项保留了姿势却撤回了赞许：手还按在按钮上，可这时没人想要那盏灯亮。

senses.title: Data that survives a restart
senses.definition: in computing, the property of data or an object remaining stored after a program, session, or device stops running
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指数据或对象在程序、会话或设备停止运行后仍被保存的性质
senses.example: The framework handles persistence by writing records to disk.
senses.exampleCN: 这个框架通过把记录写入磁盘来实现数据持久化。
senses.why: Memory is a lamp that goes out when power stops. Persistence is the design that keeps the lamp lit across the gap, the button held down by code instead of by hand.
senses.whyCN: 内存是一盏断电就灭的灯。持久化是一种设计，让灯跨过断电的间隙继续亮着，由代码而不是由手按住按钮。

senses.title: An infection that will not clear
senses.definition: the continued presence of a pathogen, symptom, or condition in the body after the expected period
senses.definitionCN: 病原体、症状或病情在预期时间之后仍继续存在于体内
senses.example: The persistence of the virus after treatment required a second course.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗之后病毒仍然存在，需要再进行一轮疗程。
senses.why: The body is a room the invader will not leave. Here persistence is not heroic but clinical: something remains where it should have stopped.
senses.whyCN: 身体是一间入侵者不肯离开的房间。这里的 persistence 不是英雄式的，而是临床的：某物停在它本该停止的地方。

senses.title: A chemical that stays in the environment
senses.titleCN: 留在环境中的化学物质
senses.definition: the ability of a substance to remain in soil, water, or living tissue for a long time without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 物质在土壤、水体或活体组织中长期存在而不分解的能力
senses.example: The persistence of the pesticide in river sediment alarmed regulators.
senses.exampleCN: 这种农药在河底沉积物中的持久残留让监管机构警觉。
senses.why: A lamp left on in an empty building: the chemical keeps standing after its usefulness is over. The word measures how long the light refuses to go out.
senses.whyCN: 像一盏留在空楼里的灯：化学物质在用处结束之后仍然站着。这个词衡量的是灯光多久不肯熄灭。

senses.title: The retina holding an image
senses.definition: the tendency of an image to remain briefly on the retina after the stimulus has moved or vanished
senses.definitionCN: 刺激移开或消失之后影像仍在视网膜上短暂停留的倾向
senses.example: Persistence of vision makes a rapid series of stills look like motion.
senses.exampleCN: 视觉暂留让一连串快速静止画面看起来像运动。
senses.why: Here the lamp is the eye itself, and the light outlives its cause by a fraction of a second. Persistence becomes the physical afterglow that cinema depends on.
senses.whyCN: 这里的灯是眼睛本身，光比它的成因多活了一瞬。persistence 成了电影所依赖的物理余辉。

senses.title: A memory that keeps returning
senses.definition: the quality of an impression or memory that stays available and keeps coming back to mind
senses.definitionCN: 印象或记忆保持可得、并不断回到心头的性质
senses.example: The persistence of that afternoon made the whole year feel unfinished.
senses.exampleCN: 那个下午挥之不去，让整年都像没有结束。
senses.why: The button is pressed by the past. Something in the mind keeps the light on long after the event, which is the emotional version of the same mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 按钮被过去按住了。心里的某样东西让灯在事件之后很久还亮着，这是同一机制的情感版本。

senses.title: A species or practice lasting
senses.titleCN: 物种或做法的长期存续
senses.definition: the continued existence of a species, language, or practice across long periods, often against pressure
senses.definitionCN: 物种、语言或做法在长时间内继续存在，常是在压力之下
senses.example: The persistence of the dialect owes much to a single village school.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方言得以存续，很大程度上归功于一所村庄学校。
senses.why: The largest lamp of all: a whole way of life stays lit. Persistence here is measured in generations, and the hand on the button is a community.
senses.whyCN: 这是最大的一盏灯：一整套生活方式持续亮着。这里的 persistence 以世代计量，按住按钮的手是一个共同体。

intro.en: Persistence comes from Latin persistentia, from persistere 'to continue steadfastly, to stand firm'. Persistere is per- 'thoroughly' plus sistere 'to stand, to take a stand'. English took the noun in the 15th century. The Latin verb sistere also gives assist, insist, resist, and consist, which is why the whole family feels like standing in different postures.
intro.cn: persistence 来自拉丁语 persistentia，出自 persistere“坚定持续、站稳”。persistere 是 per-“彻底”加 sistere“站立、站定”。英语在 15 世纪借入这个名词。拉丁动词 sistere 还产生 assist、insist、resist、consist，所以整个词族都像在不同姿势下站立。

items.en: Sistere means 'to cause to stand, to place, to stand firm'. It comes from the reconstructed PIE form *sta- 'to stand', the same root as English stand and statue.
items.cn: sistere 意为“使站立、放置、站稳”。它出自原始印欧语的重构形式 *sta-“站立”，与英语 stand（站立）、statue（雕像）同源。

items.en: Persistere adds per- 'thoroughly' to sistere: to stand through to the end, to keep one's position. Its participle persistens gives the adjective persistent.
items.cn: persistere 给 sistere 加上 per-“彻底”：站到最后、守住位置。其分词 persistens 产生形容词 persistent。

items.en: English persistence first means 'the act of persisting, constancy'. Persistency is an older doublet that survives mainly in technical usage.
items.cn: 英语 persistence 最早意为“坚持的行为、恒心”。persistency 是更早的异体，今主要存于技术用法。

items.en: The noun gains a negative shade: persistence in an opinion becomes stubbornness, the same posture seen from the other side.
items.cn: 17 世纪这个名词带上负面色彩：对某种意见的坚持变成固执，同一个姿势从另一面看。

items.en: Science adopts it: persistence of vision explains motion pictures, and the persistence of substances becomes a measure of how long they resist decay.
items.cn: 19 世纪科学采用它：视觉暂留解释电影，物质的持久性则成为衡量其抗降解能力的指标。

items.en: Computing adds data persistence, and medicine speaks of the persistence of symptoms or pathogens. The standing image now covers silicon, cells, and soil.
items.cn: 20 世纪计算机加入数据持久性，医学谈论症状或病原体的持续存在。这个“站立”的意象如今覆盖硅片、细胞与土壤。

note.en: The first group separates persistence from its verb, its adjective, and from perseverance, which looks like a twin but was formed differently. The second group compares tenacity, endurance, continuation, and obstinacy.
note.cn: 第一组把 persistence 与其动词、形容词分开，并区分看起来像双胞胎、其实构词不同的 perseverance。第二组比较坚韧、耐力、延续与固执。

entries.definition: to continue firmly or to keep existing. Persistence is the noun of that standing-still.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定继续或持续存在。persistence 是这种“站住不动”的名词形式。

entries.definition: continuing despite difficulty, or remaining for a long time. It describes the thing that stands; persistence names the standing.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍继续，或长时间保持。它描述站立的事物；persistence 命名站立本身。

entries.definition: steady persistence in a course despite difficulty. It comes from Latin perseverare, a different verb, though English uses the two almost interchangeably.
entries.definitionCN: 在道路上的稳定坚持。它出自另一个拉丁动词 perseverare，尽管英语几乎把两者当同义词使用。

entries.definition: to stand against something. It shares sistere 'stand' but reverses the direction with re- 'against'.
entries.definitionCN: 站在某物的对立面。它共享 sistere“站立”，但用 re-“对抗”把方向反过来。

entries.definition: the quality of holding firmly to a purpose or position. Its image is a hand gripping, while persistence is a body standing.
entries.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住目标或立场不放的品质。它的意象是手在紧握，而 persistence 是身体在站立。

entries.definition: the power to withstand hardship or to last. It stresses bearing pain over time rather than refusing to move.
entries.definitionCN: 承受艰难或持续长久的力量。它强调长时间忍受痛苦，而不是拒绝移动。

entries.definition: the act of carrying on after a pause or interruption. It is neutral and factual, with no praise or blame.
entries.definitionCN: 停顿或中断之后继续进行的行为。它是中性、事实性的，不含褒贬。

entries.definition: stubborn refusal to change course. It is the negative reading of persistence, with the virtue removed.
entries.definitionCN: 顽固拒绝改变方向。它是对 persistence 的负面读法，抽掉了美德成分。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: sistere 'stand', per- 'thoroughly', the sistere family (assist, insist, resist), the 15th-century noun, and the perseverance contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：sistere“站立”、per-“彻底”、sistere 词族（assist、insist、resist）、15 世纪的名词，以及与 perseverance 的对比。

normal.en: Sistere is 'to stand': persistence is standing thoroughly, per- 'through', until the difficulty passes or gives way.
normal.cn: sistere 是“站立”：persistence 就是“彻底站住”，站到困难过去或让路为止。

normal.en: Assist, insist, resist, and consist all contain sistere: each is a different way of standing — beside, upon, against, together.
normal.cn: assist、insist、resist、consist 都含 sistere：每一种都是一种站法——旁边、上面、对面、一起。

normal.en: The same posture can be praised as persistence or blamed as obstinacy; the word alone does not decide which.
normal.cn: 同一个姿势可以被赞为坚持，也可以被斥为固执；单凭这个词决定不了哪一种。

normal.en: Perseverance is the near twin from perseverare; the meaning overlaps, but the Latin verb behind it is different.
normal.cn: perseverance 是来自 perseverare 的近亲双胞胎；意义重叠，背后的拉丁动词却不同。

normal.en: Computing keeps the lamp lit across a restart; that is data persistence, the same button held by code.
normal.cn: 计算机让灯跨过重启继续亮着；这就是数据持久化，同一颗按钮由代码按住。

abstract.en: A hand on a button in a dark room is not hope; it is the refusal to let the dark have the last word.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中按着按钮的手不是希望；它只是拒绝让黑暗说了算。

abstract.en: A tradition survives because each generation stands in the same place for a moment before stepping aside.
abstract.cn: 传统得以存续，是因为每一代都在同一个地方站一会儿，然后才让开。

abstract.en: A chemical that will not decay is a guest who never learns to leave.
abstract.cn: 不会降解的化学物质，是一个永远学不会离开的客人。

examples.en: Her persistence finally convinced the publisher to read the manuscript.
examples.cn: 她的坚持最终说服出版方读了那份手稿。

examples.en: The persistence of the drought forced the town to ration water.
examples.cn: 干旱持续不退，迫使小镇实行配给供水。

examples.en: The database guarantees persistence even if the power fails.
examples.cn: 即使断电，这个数据库也能保证数据持久保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破西斯特恩斯」——破开阻力，像“西”装骑士一样一站到底，手一直按着不松 → persistence 坚持不懈；持续存在（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 persistere「坚定持续、站稳」，由 per-「彻底」+ sistere「站立」构成（*sta-「站立」词根），名词为 persistentia；后缀 -ence（拉丁 -entia）表状态。核心是「一只手一直按在按钮上，灯始终没灭」。同族含 persist、persistent、persistently；perseverance 出自另一动词 perseverare，resist、insist、assist 则共享 sistere 但前缀不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of persistence all describe a hand that keeps the lamp lit. What changes is why it stays: difficulty, mere duration, stubbornness, a restart, a pathogen, soil, the retina, memory, or a whole community across generations.
sensesIntro.cn: persistence 的九个义项都描述一只让灯持续亮着的手。变化的是它为什么还按着：困难、单纯的延续、固执、一次重启、病原体、土壤、视网膜、记忆，还是一个跨越世代的共同体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand held on a button, so that the lamp never goes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手一直按在按钮上，那盏灯始终没有灭。

branches.en: THE HAND AND ITS SHADOW: the praised virtue of continuing against difficulty, and the same posture read as stubbornness.
branches.cn: 手与它的影子：面对困难继续前行的受赞美德，以及同一姿势被读成固执。

branches.en: MERE CONTINUANCE: things, traditions, and species that simply fail to stop.
branches.cn: 单纯的延续：只是没有停下来的事物、传统与物种。

branches.en: TECHNICAL REMAINDER: data that survives a restart, and chemicals that refuse to break down.
branches.cn: 技术性的留存：挺过重启的数据，以及拒绝分解的化学物质。

branches.en: THE BODY'S GUEST: a pathogen or symptom that stays after it should have left.
branches.cn: 身体里的客人：本该离开之后仍留下的病原体或症状。

branches.en: THE AFTERGLOW: an image left on the retina, and a memory that keeps returning to mind.
branches.cn: 余辉：留在视网膜上的影像，以及不断回到心头的记忆。

intro.en: Persistence is persist plus -ence, from Latin -entia, a state noun. Persist is Latin persistere, per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'stand'. The same sistere carries assist, insist, resist, and consist, so the family reads like a set of standing postures.
intro.cn: persistence 是 persist 加 -ence（拉丁 -entia，状态名词）。persist 是拉丁 persistere，即 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站立”。同一个 sistere 还带着 assist、insist、resist、consist，所以这个词族读起来像一组站立的姿势。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is sistere 'to stand, place', persistere 'to stand firm', and persistentia 'constancy'. The root is PIE *sta- 'stand', which also gives English stand, stable, and statue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 sistere“站立、放置”、persistere“站稳”、persistentia“恒心”。词根是原始印欧语 *sta-“站立”，它也产生英语 stand（站立）、stable（稳固）与 statue（雕像）。

items.meaning: the state of standing firm or continuing
items.meaningCN: 站稳或持续的状态（-ence 状态名词）
items.example: Persistence is often worth more than talent.
items.exampleCN: 坚持往往比天赋更值钱。

items.meaningCN: 站稳、持续（per- 彻底 + sistere 站立）
items.example: The problem persisted for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题持续了十年。

items.meaningCN: 站稳的；持续的（-ent 分词形容词词尾）
items.example: A persistent cough sent him to the clinic.
items.exampleCN: 持续的咳嗽让他去了诊所。

items.example: She persistently asked for the records.
items.exampleCN: 她一再要求查看记录。

items.example: The coating's persistency was tested in salt water.
items.exampleCN: 这种涂层的持久性在盐水中接受了测试。

items.meaning: to stand by someone, hence to help
items.meaningCN: 站在某人旁边，因而表示帮助（ad- 向 + sistere 站立）
items.example: A nurse assisted during the procedure.
items.exampleCN: 一名护士在手术过程中协助。

items.meaning: to stand upon something, hence to demand
items.meaningCN: 站在某物之上，因而表示坚持要求（in- 在上 + sistere 站立）
items.example: He insisted on paying for the meal.
items.exampleCN: 他坚持要付这顿饭钱。

items.meaningCN: 站在对立面；抵抗（re- 对抗 + sistere 站立）
items.example: The material resists heat well.
items.exampleCN: 这种材料耐热性很好。

items.meaningCN: 不长时间留存的（non- 否定）
items.example: Nonpersistent chemicals break down within weeks.
items.exampleCN: 非持久性化学物质在数周内分解。

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to stand, to place, to stand firm

definition_zh: 人口结构变化；出生、死亡与迁移带来的年龄、家庭与地区分布变动
definition_en: a shift over time in the size, age, distribution or composition of a population
core_image: 海边小城的年轻人外出打工，学校合并、产科关闭，老年人口比例逐年上升，统计图上的曲线明显转向
scene: 这里指「人口结构变化」。 The shrinking schools and rising median age are signs of rapid demographic change in the coastal town.
sceneCN: 此处指「人口年龄与家庭结构在较短时间内明显改变」（第 1 个义项：人口构成随时间发生的整体变动）；句意为学校缩减与年龄中位数上升，是这座海边小城人口结构快速变化的迹象。可辨识物件：空荡的教室、合并的校牌、关闭的产科门口、统计折线图。

pos.zh: 人口结构变化（可数或不可数）
人口变动过程（统计与政策语境）

senses.title: A shift in population composition
senses.definition: a change over time in the size, age structure or make-up of a population
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内人口规模、年龄结构或构成成分的变化
senses.example: The shrinking schools and rising median age are signs of rapid demographic change in the coastal town.
senses.exampleCN: 学校缩减与年龄中位数上升，是这座海边小城人口结构快速变化的迹象。
senses.why: Demographic comes from Greek demos 'people' plus graphein 'to write', so demographic change is literally a change in what is written down about a people.
senses.whyCN: demographic 来自希腊 demos「人民」加 graphein「书写」，因此这个短语字面就是「关于人群的记述发生了变化」。

senses.title: A shift in births and deaths
senses.titleCN: 出生与死亡结构的变化
senses.definition: a change in birth rates, death rates or life expectancy that alters the balance of a population
senses.definitionCN: 出生率、死亡率或预期寿命的变化，改变了一个人口的平衡
senses.example: Falling births and longer lives drove demographic change across the whole province.
senses.exampleCN: 出生减少与寿命延长推动了全省的人口变化。
senses.why: The field began by counting births and deaths, so the phrase first named the change in those two rates.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科最初统计出生与死亡，因此这个短语首先指这两项比率的变化。

senses.title: A shift caused by migration
senses.definition: a change produced by people moving into or out of an area rather than by natural increase alone
senses.definitionCN: 由人口迁入或迁出而非仅由自然增长造成的变化
senses.example: The departure of young workers produced a demographic change that no birth policy could reverse.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻工人的外流造成了一种任何生育政策都无法逆转的人口变化。
senses.why: Migration changes who lives where, so it became one of the standard engines listed under the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 迁移改变谁住在哪里，因此成为这一短语下列举的标准动因之一。

senses.title: Population aging
senses.definition: the part of the shift in which the share of older people rises and the share of children falls
senses.definitionCN: 人口变化中老年人口比例上升、儿童比例下降的那一部分
senses.example: Demographic change in the town showed up first as a shortage of primary pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的人口变化最早表现为小学生源不足。
senses.why: Aging is the most visible result of long-term changes in births and deaths, and it is often named by the same phrase.
senses.whyCN: 老龄化是出生与死亡长期变化最可见的结果，因此常被同一短语概括。

senses.title: A shift in household structure
senses.definition: a change in household size and type, such as smaller families, single households or later marriage
senses.definitionCN: 家庭规模与类型的变化，如家庭变小、单人户增多或婚龄推迟
senses.example: Demographic change reduced the average household to two people within a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 人口变化在一代人的时间里把平均家庭规模降到两人。
senses.why: Counting people also means counting how they live together, so the phrase extends from individuals to households.
senses.whyCN: 清点人口也意味着清点他们如何共同生活，因此这个短语从个人延伸到家庭。

senses.title: A policy challenge
senses.titleCN: 作为政策挑战的人口变化
senses.definition: the same shift considered as a problem that governments must plan for in schools, pensions and housing
senses.definitionCN: 把同一变动视为政府必须在学校、养老金与住房上作出规划的问题
senses.example: The ministry published a plan in response to demographic change along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 该部发布计划，以应对沿海地区的人口变化。
senses.why: Politicians borrowed the term because a change in age structure forces decisions about budgets and services.
senses.whyCN: 政治人物借用这个术语，因为年龄结构的变化会迫使预算与服务作出决定。

senses.title: A measurable statistical trend
senses.definition: the numerical trend itself, as shown by censuses, birth records and migration figures
senses.definitionCN: 由普查、出生记录与迁移数字显示出来的数量趋势本身
senses.example: The census chart made three decades of demographic change visible in one line.
senses.exampleCN: 普查图表用一条线把三十年的人口变化显示出来。
senses.why: The phrase is used for the data series as well as the event, because the trend is what analysts actually measure.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既指事件，也指数据序列，因为分析者实际测量的正是趋势。

senses.title: Regional variation
senses.definition: the uneven pattern of the shift, with some districts growing while neighbouring ones lose people
senses.definitionCN: 变化在不同地区的不均衡格局，一些区在增长，邻近的区却在流失人口
senses.example: Demographic change in the capital looked nothing like the change in the hill villages.
senses.exampleCN: 首都的人口变化与山村的人口变化看上去完全不同。
senses.why: The same national trend hits local labour markets differently, so the phrase also names the uneven map rather than one uniform wave.
senses.whyCN: 同一国家趋势对各地劳动力市场的冲击不同，因此这个短语也指那张不均衡的地图，而非一道均匀的浪。

senses.title: A generational turnover
senses.definition: the replacement of one generation by the next, with different habits, expectations and household forms
senses.definitionCN: 一代人被下一代人替代，并带来习惯、期待与家庭形式的差异
senses.example: Demographic change in the electorate reshaped the party's promises.
senses.exampleCN: 选民人口的变化重塑了这个政党的承诺。
senses.why: Turnover is the long-run form of the same shift, so the phrase can name a change of generations rather than of totals.
senses.whyCN: 代际更替是同一变动的长期形态，因此这个短语也可指代际变化而非总量变化。

intro.en: Demographic change joins demographic, from Greek demos 'people' and graphein 'to write', with the English word change, from Latin cambire through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由「人口的」与「变化」两个词组合；前者来自希腊 demos「人民」与 graphein「书写」，后者经古法语来自拉丁 cambire。年代均为约数。

items.en: Demos meant 'the people, the common people', and it supplied the first element of demography.
items.cn: demos 意为「人民、平民」，提供人口学的第一个成分。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, to draw'. The combining form -graphia named a written description of a subject.
items.cn: graphein 意为「书写、描画」，组合成分 -graphia 指对某主题的书面描述。

items.en: Change came through Old French from Latin cambire 'to exchange, to barter', which developed the sense 'to become different'.
items.cn: change 经古法语来自拉丁 cambire「交换、以物易物」，逐步发展出「变得不同」的意思。

items.en: Demography as a discipline took shape in the nineteenth century, and demographic change became its standard phrase for shifts in population structure.
items.cn: 人口学在十九世纪成形，这一短语成为其指人口结构变动的标准说法。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase spread into planning, pensions and migration debates, widening beyond the counting office.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个短语扩散到规划、养老金与移民争论，超出统计机构的范围。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use of the exact phrase is not precisely dated, and the deeper origin of cambire is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个确切短语的最早用例缺乏精确年代，cambire 的更深来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds terms built on the same population root or the same change word; group two holds terms for related population events and measures.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「人口」词根或同带「变化」一词的术语；第二组是关于相关人口事件与测量的说法。

entries.definition: Means relating to population statistics; the phrase adds the idea of a shift over time.
entries.definitionCN: 意为与人口统计有关的；短语加上的是随时间变动的意思。

entries.definition: The study of populations; demographic change is one of its central objects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人口的学科；人口变化是它的核心对象之一。

entries.definition: The statistical facts about a population, or the customer groups defined by them.
entries.definitionCN: 关于人口的统计事实，或由此划分的客户群体。

entries.definition: Any shift in norms, institutions or behaviour; demographic change is specifically about population structure.
entries.definitionCN: 规范、制度或行为的任何变动；人口变化专指人口结构。

entries.definition: A general phrase for people moving or changing in number; demographic change is the technical equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 指人口移动或数量变化的一般说法；人口变化是其技术对应语。

entries.definition: The act of moving from one place to another; it is one cause of demographic change, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一个地方迁到另一个地方，是人口变化的一个原因，而非全部。

entries.definition: A population with a rising share of older people; it is often the most visible face of the wider change.
entries.definitionCN: 老年人口比例上升的人口；常是更大变化最可见的一面。

entries.definition: The official counting of a population; it measures change but is not the change itself.
entries.definitionCN: 官方对人口的清点；它测量变化，但本身不是变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek demos 'people' plus graphein 'write' gives demographic: a written account of a people.
normal.cn: 希腊 demos「人民」加 graphein「书写」构成 demographic：对人民的书面记述。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the sense: rapid demographic change, demographic change and aging, the pace of change.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出词义：快速的人口变化、人口变化与老龄化、变化速度。

normal.en: The family runs demography, demographic, demographer and demographics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 demography、demographic、demographer 与 demographics。

normal.en: Change has its own root, Latin cambire 'to exchange', so the phrase joins two separate word families.
normal.cn: change 有自己的词根，即拉丁 cambire「交换」，因此这个短语连接了两个不同词族。

normal.en: The phrase names both the event and the statistical trend that measures it.
normal.cn: 这个短语既指事件，也指测量该事件的统计趋势。

abstract.en: Picture a school corridor where the desks are removed one row at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一条学校走廊，课桌一排一排被搬走。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a graph bending slowly, then suddenly, across a decade.
abstract.cn: 想象图上一条线在十年间先缓后急地弯下去。

abstract.en: Picture a village where the only sound at noon is a radio playing to empty rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄，正午唯一的声音是唱给空屋子的收音机。

examples.en: Housing plans must account for demographic change, not only for current demand.
examples.cn: 住房规划必须考虑人口变化，而不只是当前需求。

examples.en: The province's demographic change was driven more by migration than by births.
examples.cn: 该省的人口变化更多由迁移而非出生推动。

examples.en: Researchers used census data to chart two decades of demographic change.
examples.cn: 研究者用普查数据绘制了二十年的人口变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「demo（人民）+ graphic（书写）+ change（变化）」——人民构成的记录变了 → 人口结构变化

root: demographic 来自希腊 demos「人民」与 graphein「书写」；change 经古法语来自拉丁 cambire「交换」。该短语是现代社会科学的合成术语，最早书证年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one shift: the whole composition, births and deaths, migration, aging, households, policy, measurable trend, regional unevenness and generational turnover.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟随着同一场变动：整体构成、出生与死亡、迁移、老龄化、家庭、政策、可测趋势、地区不均衡与代际更替。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a graph line bending across a decade while the desks leave a school one row at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：十年间一条曲线弯下去，同时学校里的课桌一排排被搬走。

branches.en: COUNT AND BALANCE: the composition changes because births and deaths change first.
branches.cn: 清点与平衡：构成的变化，先从出生与死亡的变化开始。

branches.en: MIGRATION: people moving in or out changes the count without any birth or death.
branches.cn: 迁移：人口迁入或迁出，不靠出生死亡也能改变数字。

branches.en: AGE AND GENERATION: aging and generational turnover are the same shift seen in cohorts.
branches.cn: 年龄与代际：老龄化与代际更替是同一变动在同代人身上的显现。

branches.en: HOUSEHOLDS: counting people also counts how they live together.
branches.cn: 家庭：清点人口也在清点他们如何共同生活。

branches.en: MEASURE AND POLICY: the trend is measured, felt unevenly by region, and answered by budgets.
branches.cn: 测量与政策：趋势被测量，在地区间感受不均，并由预算作出回应。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective with a Latin-derived noun, and both halves have their own derived forms.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的形容词与拉丁来源的名词组合起来，两半各有派生形式。

latinIntro.en: Greek demos and graphein supply demographic; Latin cambire supplies change; English added demography and demographer.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 demos 与 graphein 提供 demographic；拉丁 cambire 提供 change；英语又造出 demography 与 demographer。

items.exampleCN: 第一个成分指被清点的人民。

items.example: The second element names the written record.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分指书面记录。

items.example: Demographic data drove the plan.
items.exampleCN: 人口统计数据推动了这项计划。

items.example: Demography began with parish registers.
items.exampleCN: 人口学始于教区登记簿。

items.example: The demographer projected the decline.
items.exampleCN: 这位人口学家预测了下降趋势。

items.exampleCN: 这个品牌研究了其客户人口构成。

items.example: The town changed quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这座城镇变化很快。

items.example: The phrase names the trend.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语命名这一趋势。

items.exampleCN: 出生率保持不变。
